industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Neutral, from Overweight, on the row's own written condition ('to C if Brent is read under $85 or the industry's relative strength falls to C'): the relative strength leg fired. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: C now, A prior at the industry (B at last week's reading), with Downstream distribution A and Upstream A against Services D, Agriculture D and Metals and mining F. The price leg moved the same way without firing: oil stayed below $100 as traders weighed Iran (Dow Jones Newswires, 5 November), against Brent near $115 at the 30-Oct-26 read, with hopes of a Middle East de-escalation (LBBW, 6 November). Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). The hedge this row was held for is being unwound in the price, and the industry letter was lending 30% of its weight to three sectors the market is selling. The view stays where the evidence is, in the sector rows: Downstream distribution Double Overweight, Upstream and Services Overweight, unchanged. No memo carried a congruence line this week. Counter-case: Iran supply risk is the one skew a source named for oil, and the two largest energy sectors still read A on relative strength, so this takes weight off the Pool's 18 upstream and downstream names a week before the tape might turn back. Back to B if the industry's relative strength returns to B with oil holding its level; the sector rows go to Neutral only if Brent is read under $85.

sector.key: P.3. Energy - services and engineering contractors
sector.why: Overweight, carried against the tape for another week, and now the row in the table most exposed to being wrong. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: D now, C prior; the conditions for Neutral (Brent read under $85, or relative strength at F) are not met: oil is below $100 (Dow Jones Newswires, 5 November), down from near $115 at the 30-Oct-26 read, and no Brent level was read. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). Held on Kepler Cheuvreux's structural read of 29 October (vessels booked 18 to 24 months, pricing holding regardless of spot crude), now two weeks old and not contradicted; the industry letter above it goes to Neutral this week, so the sector letter carries the view alone. No stock in this sector is in the Pool this week. Counter-case: services are the most operationally geared end of energy and oil has lost roughly $15 on de-escalation hopes. To C if Brent is read under $85 or relative strength falls to F; to A only with relative strength back at B.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
